  - How have cinematic representations and genres addressing transgender lives in Middle Eastern and North African cinema evolved from state-funded and postcolonial national cinemas (mid-20th century) through the 1990s–2010s arthouse/independent waves to the contemporary festival and streaming era (2015–2026), and what does a comparative close reading of at least three films from different countries and decades—framed by trans theory (e.g., Butler, Halberstam, Preciado, trans studies) and film theory (melodrama, documentary modes, queer/feminist film theory, affect)—reveal about changing aesthetics, authorship, censorship, and audience formation?
